details:
**Kaaba**
The cube-shaped shrine at the center of Mecca's Great Mosque and the most sacred site in Islam. It is draped in the kiswah, a black cloth embroidered in gold, and its interior is cleaned with rosewater twice a year. Muslims believe Abraham and Ishmael built it.

**Hajj and tawaf**
The hajj, the annual pilgrimage to Mecca during the month of Dhu al-Hijjah, is the fifth Pillar of Islam, required once in a lifetime of every Muslim who is able to make it. Its central rite is tawaf, walking seven times counterclockwise around the Kaaba, with men taking the first three circuits at a quicker pace. During hajj, Mecca's population of about two million roughly doubles.

**Black Stone**
A sacred stone set in a silver frame in the eastern corner of the Kaaba, which pilgrims try to kiss, touch, or point to during tawaf. Tradition says it was originally white and turned black from the sins of those who touched it. The Qarmatians stole it in 930 and returned it in 952.

**Well of Zamzam**
A sacred well near the Kaaba that, according to tradition, God made spring up to save Hagar (Hajar) and her infant son Ishmael from dying of thirst in the desert. Pilgrims drink its water during the hajj.

**Sa'i between Safa and Marwah**
The hajj and umrah rite of walking or running seven times between the two small hills of Safa and Marwah, now enclosed within the Great Mosque. It re-enacts Hagar's frantic search for water for Ishmael.

**Stoning of the Devil**
A hajj ritual at Mina, outside Mecca, in which pilgrims throw seven pebbles at each of three pillars (now walls) that represent Satan tempting Abraham. The Jamarat Bridge was built to manage the dangerous crowds at this rite. Afterward, pilgrims sacrifice an animal for Eid al-Adha, with the meat going to the poor, and men shave their heads (halq) while women trim their hair (taqsir).

**Ihram**
The state of ritual purity pilgrims enter at boundary stations (miqat) before hajj or umrah. Men wear two unstitched, unhemmed white sheets, and pilgrims must avoid acts such as hunting, cutting their hair, and vanity. They recite the Talbiyah prayer, "Here I am, O God, here I am."

**Hijrah**
Muhammad's emigration in 622 from Mecca to Yathrib, which was renamed Medina, to escape persecution by the Quraysh. Ali slept in Muhammad's bed to deceive the assassins while Muhammad escaped with Abu Bakr. The event marks year one of the Islamic lunar calendar (AH).

**Qibla**
The direction of the Kaaba in Mecca, which Muslims face during their five daily prayers. In a mosque it is shown by the mihrab, a niche in the qibla wall.

**Quraysh and Hubal**
The Quraysh were the tribe that controlled Mecca and its shrine in Muhammad's time, and they at first opposed him. Before Islam, the Kaaba housed some 360 idols, chief among them Hubal, whose idol was used for divination with arrows. Muhammad cleared the idols after conquering Mecca with about ten thousand men in 630.

**Masjid al-Haram**
The Great Mosque of Mecca, which surrounds the Kaaba and is the largest mosque in the world. Non-Muslims are forbidden to enter Mecca.

**Maqam Ibrahim**
The "Station of Abraham," a stone near the Kaaba kept in a gold-colored case. It bears footprints said to have been left by Abraham as he stood on it while building the Kaaba.

**Mount Arafat**
A hill and plain outside Mecca where pilgrims stand in prayerful vigil on the ninth of Dhu al-Hijjah, the climax of the hajj. It commemorates Muhammad's Farewell Sermon, delivered on the Mount of Mercy (Jabal al-Rahmah). Pilgrims then spend the night at Muzdalifah.

**Umrah**
The "lesser pilgrimage" to Mecca, which shares rites such as ihram, tawaf, and sa'i with the hajj. Unlike hajj, it can be performed at any time of year and is not obligatory.

**Birthplace of Muhammad and the Cave of Hira**
Muhammad was born in Mecca in the "Year of the Elephant," named for a failed attack on the city by the Abyssinian ruler Abraha, whose army included an elephant. In the Cave of Hira, on a mountain just outside the city, he received his first revelation. His wife Khadijah and uncle Abu Talib died in Mecca in the "Year of Sorrow."
